body.statement: Under admissible-cell interior positivity, every denominator admitted by the branch positivity ledger is strictly positive at \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\). Selector correction introduces no division beyond initialization of a supported context kernel, whose denominator is \(p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}}p_H(v,s)>0\) for \(s\in H\). A reachable fixing denominator \(m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}\) is positive because its ledger certificate writes its numerator as a nonempty sum of positive admissible-cell probabilities and its inherited denominator as a product of earlier positive entries. After cancellation and sign normalization, every rational-elimination denominator is positive because eligibility requires its exact factorization into a positive rational constant, earlier selector or fixing denominators, and nonempty sums of branch-reachable positive kernel cells. Consequently \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\) for every returned formula branch. The lemma supplies no uniform numerical lower bound.
body.justification: The ledger separates positivity genuinely implied by the restricted-support interior from arbitrary nonzero rational polynomials whose signs would otherwise be uncontrolled.
body.gap: Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash rebuild positive gID witnesses, but they do not state this structural-zero and fixed-selector-support denominator ledger.
body.consumer: Certificate verification can audit each division locally and establish that a returned circuit covers the entire compatible fixed-support image without imposing a common overlap constant.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) and set \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\).  We induct over the finite canonical order in which denominators are admitted to the branch ledger.

For a context \(s\in H\), the initialization denominator is
\[
 p_H(S=s)=
 \sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v,s).
\tag{1}
\]
Exact support, \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\), makes the left side positive.  Equivalently, the sum is nonempty and each of its structurally admissible summands is positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  Selector rewriting itself introduces no further division by \(\textnormal{def:selector-transition}\).

Suppose all entries earlier than an admitted fixing margin are positive.  Its eligibility certificate, required by \(\textnormal{def:fixing-transition}\), writes it as
\[
 m_{s,W}(p_H)
 =\frac{\sum_{c\in B}p_H(c)}
 {\prod_{j\in J}d_{H,j}(p_H)},
\tag{2}
\]
where \(B\subseteq\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\) is nonempty and every \(j\in J\) precedes this margin.  The numerator of (2) is strictly positive by admissible-cell interior positivity, and the denominator is strictly positive by the induction hypothesis; the empty-product case equals one.  Hence \(m_{s,W}(p_H)>0\).

After cancellation and sign normalization, an admitted rational-elimination denominator has, by \(\textnormal{def:elimination-transition}\), an exact ledger factorization
\[
 d(p_H)=r
 \prod_{j\in J_0}d_{H,j}(p_H)
 \prod_{k\in J_1}
 \left\{\sum_{c\in B_k}K_k(p_H,c)\right\},
 \qquad r\in\mathbb Q_{>0},
\tag{3}
\]
where the entries indexed by \(J_0\) are earlier selector or fixing denominators, every \(B_k\) is nonempty, and the ledger certifies each displayed kernel cell as branch-reachable and positive.  Every factor in (3) is therefore positive: this follows from the induction hypothesis for the first product and from the certified positivity and nonemptiness for each sum in the second product.  Thus \(d(p_H)>0\).

Finite induction proves that every member of \(\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}}\) is positive at \(p_H\), while (1) and admissible-cell interior positivity establish all branch-required cell inequalities.  The definition of \(\mathfrak D_H\) now gives \(O_H(\theta)\in\mathfrak D_H\).  Since \(\theta\) was arbitrary,
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\]
Every step is pointwise at the chosen \(\theta\); no common positive lower bound was introduced.
